theorem.statement:
Assume that \(K\) is row-stochastic, that \((L,K)\) is fixed before observing \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and that
\[
d_K(A)\geq \pi(A)\qquad
(\varnothing\neq A\subseteq\Omega).
\]
Fix a realized assignment \(x_0\in\Omega\), a count \(r\in\{0,\ldots,N\}\), and a threshold \(c\in\mathbb R\).  Under fixed peer exposure, imputability, and the fixed rank-statistic rule, the following finite formulation is exact.  Introduce the \(2N\) variables \(z_{ua}=\theta_u(a,e)\).  Enumerate \(h\in\{0,1\}^{U}\) with \(\sum_u h_u\leq r\), and enumerate
\[
\lambda_{xuv}\in\{-1,0,1\},qquad
x\in\Omega,\quad 1\leq u<v\leq N,
\]
where \(h_u=1\) represents \(z_{u1}-z_{u0}>c\) and \(\lambda_{xuv}\) is the sign of \(z_{u,Z_u(x)}-z_{v,Z_v(x)}\).  For each of the at most
\(2^N3^{m\binom N2}\) labels, impose the observation equalities, the indicated strict or weak effect inequalities, and the indicated sign equalities or inequalities.  A label having strict rows \(a_j^{\mathsf T}z<b_j\) is feasible if and only if the auxiliary linear program
\[
\max_{z,\varepsilon}\ \varepsilon
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
a_j^{\mathsf T}z\leq b_j-\varepsilon\ (j),
\quad Cz\leq d,
\quad Ez=f,
\quad 0\leq\varepsilon\leq1
\]
has optimum strictly positive; if there is no strict row, ordinary feasibility is used.  The fixed tie rule turns each feasible \(\lambda\) into ranks and hence into constants \(t_\lambda(x)=T(x,Y_\theta(x))\).  Consequently
\[
p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(x_0)
=max_{(h,\lambda)\ {
m feasible}}
\sum_{y\in\Omega}K(x_0,y)
\mathbf 1\{t_\lambda(y)\geq t_\lambda(x_0)\}.
\]
If \(\Theta_{r,c}(x_0,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\neq\varnothing\), the maximum is attained and the feasibility program returns an optimizing compatible schedule; otherwise the formulation returns an infeasibility certificate.  With rational or real-algebraic representations of \(K\), \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(c\), \(\alpha\), and the finite rank-score table, this is a terminating exact computation.  For arbitrary unspecified real inputs it is a finite formulation in ideal exact-real arithmetic, not a Turing-algorithm claim.  The same finite formulation applies to, and therefore exactly solves, the three-assignment, two-unit shared-coordinate pattern.

For \(1\leq k\leq N\), define in the extended real line
\[
b_k(x_0;\alpha)
=\sup\{c\in\mathbb R:
p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{N-k,c}(x_0)\leq\alpha\},
\qquad \sup\varnothing=-\infty.
\]
The nested finite-cell computations give the exact projection identity
\[
\ell_k(e;\alpha)=b_k(X;\alpha),
\qquad k=1,\ldots,N,
\]
where \(\inf\varnothing=+infty\).  In particular,
\[
\Pr_{X\sim\pi}\!\left\{
\tau_{(k)}(e)\geq\ell_k(e;\alpha)
\text{ for every }k=1,\ldots,N
\right\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
If the inverted region is empty because rejected thresholds are unbounded, the finite set of attainable rank-score patterns stabilizes for large \(c\); this forces rejection at \(r=N\), and hence \(b_k=+\infty\) for every \(k\), so the displayed projection identity remains valid.

Under no interference, the order-statistic equivalence
\[
\sum_{u\in U}\mathbf 1\{\tau_u(e)>c\}\leq r
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\tau_{(N-r)}(e)\leq c
\qquad(r<N)
\]
is exact, and partition kernels retain finite-sample validity.  Nevertheless, the frozen assignment-specific schedule score does not exactly recover either the Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix adjusted-outcome statistic or the Su--Li multiple-choice-knapsack statistic.  In the two-unit, one-treated partition example with \(\phi(q)=q\), potential outcomes \((1,3)\) for unit one and \((0,2)\) for unit two, and observed assignment treating unit one, the frozen bounded-null value at \((r,c)=(0,2)\) is \(1\), whereas the Caughey adjusted-outcome upper-tail value is \(1/2\); the one-stratum Su--Li clause contains the same obstruction.  Thus the exact network schedule reduction and simultaneous projection are positive, but the requested exact recovery and strict-extension claims for those two comparator algorithms are false.
theorem.proof_tex:
Write \(x_0\) for the realized value of \(X\).  By fixed peer exposure, every focal outcome used on the fiber has the form
\[
Y_\theta(x)_u=z_{u,Z_u(x)},
\qquad z_{ua}:=\theta_u(a,e),
\]
and observation consistency is precisely
\[
z_{u,Z_u(x_0)}=Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_u,
\qquad u\in U.
\tag{1}
\]
Coordinates of \(\theta\) outside exposure \(e\) do not enter any fiber score and may be completed arbitrarily.  This uses the fixed-exposure assumption, while legal imputability ensures that every coordinate displayed above is available in every comparison used by \(T\).

For each \(u\), split the real line into the two disjoint cases
\[
h_u=1:\ z_{u1}-z_{u0}>c,
\qquad
h_u=0:\ z_{u1}-z_{u0}\leq c.
\tag{2}
\]
Then the bounded null is exactly \(\sum_u h_u\leq r\), including equality at the threshold in the \(h_u=0\) case.  For each \(x\in\Omega\) and \(u<v\), split the difference
\[
D_{xuv}:=z_{u,Z_u(x)}-z_{v,Z_v(x)}
\tag{3}
\]
into \(D_{xuv}<0\), \(D_{xuv}=0\), or \(D_{xuv}>0\).  Equations (1)--(3), over every binary label \(h\) and ternary label \(\lambda\), form a disjoint cover of the compatible schedule set.  There are no more than
\[
2^N3^{|\Omega|\binom N2}=2^N3^{m\binom N2}
\tag{4}
\]
such labels.  Reusing the same \(z_{ua}\) in (1)--(3) across every assignment enforces all shared-potential-outcome equalities; no product relaxation has been made.

Fix one label.  After reversing the sign of each strict lower inequality if necessary, write its strict rows as \(a_j^{\mathsf T}z<b_j\), its weak rows as \(Cz\leq d\), and its equalities as \(Ez=f\).  If the cell contains \(z^\star\), the finitely many strict slacks have a positive minimum \(\delta\).  Hence \((z^\star,\min\{1,\delta\})\) is feasible for the auxiliary program and its optimum is positive.  Conversely, any feasible pair with \(\varepsilon>0\) obeys every original strict row.  Thus
\[
\{z:a_j^{\mathsf T}z<b_j, Cz\leq d, Ez=f\}\neq\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\varepsilon^\star>0.
\tag{5}
\]
When the set of strict rows is empty, (5) is replaced by feasibility of the displayed closed system.  This proves the feasibility certificate without imposing artificial bounds or a big-\(M\) constant.

The ternary signs in (3), together with the predeclared deterministic tie order, fix the complete rank vector at every assignment.  Because \(T\) is a fixed rank statistic, it is constant on each such cell; denote its value at \(x\) by \(t_\lambda(x)\).  The kernel tail value on the cell is therefore the constant
\[
W_\lambda(x_0)
:=\sum_{y\in\Omega}K(x_0,y)
\mathbf 1\{t_\lambda(y)\geq t_\lambda(x_0)\}.
\tag{6}
\]
The cells cover \(\Theta_{r,c}(x_0,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\), so taking the supremum in the definition of \(p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}\) gives
\[
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{r,c}(x_0,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})}p_K(x_0;s_\theta)
=\max_{(h,\lambda):\,\text{cell nonempty}}W_\lambda(x_0).
\tag{7}
\]
There are finitely many terms in (7).  A nonempty maximizing cell supplies a feasible \(z\) by (5), and arbitrary completion outside \(e\) supplies an optimizing schedule \(\theta\).  If no cell is feasible, the compatible set is empty and the enumeration certifies that fact.  In particular, (1)--(7) retain the repeated coordinates in the three-state, two-unit pattern, so that pattern is solved exactly; its claimed minimality and connected shared-coordinate structure are supplied by the established minimal-coupling proposition.

For rational or real-algebraic inputs, every comparison and arithmetic operation in (1)--(7) is exact.  A direct elimination algorithm terminates: substitute equality pivots, eliminate one inequality variable at a time by pairing every lower bound with every upper bound, decide the resulting finitely many algebraic signs, and back-substitute.  Applying the same elimination to \(\varepsilon\) decides whether a feasible value with \(\varepsilon>0\) exists and constructs one.  Thus finite enumeration plus elimination is a Turing procedure for exactly represented rational or algebraic data.  With arbitrary real constants lacking finite representations, equations (1)--(7) remain an exact finite reduction only in an ideal ordered-real computation model.

The same argument computes the continuum inversion with finitely many operations.  Treat \(c\) as one additional variable in (2).  For each fixed label, eliminating \(z\) projects its relatively open polyhedron onto an interval in the \(c\)-line, with open or closed endpoints recorded by the slack test (5).  Linear optimization or the just-described elimination computes its algebraic endpoints.  The finitely many interval endpoints and the finitely many values (6) partition the line into finitely many points and intervals on which \(p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(x_0)\) is constant.  Exact endpoint evaluation therefore computes every \(b_k(x_0;\alpha)\).

We next prove that these computed endpoints are exactly the projections of \(\mathcal C_\alpha\), including the empty-region case.  For \(j=1,\ldots,N\), put
\[
\mathcal R_j:=\{c:p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{N-j,c}(x_0)\leq\alpha\},
\qquad b_j:=\sup\mathcal R_j.
\tag{8}
\]
Increasing \(r\) enlarges \(\Theta_{r,c}\), so it cannot decrease the worst-case value.  Hence, if \(j\leq k\), then
\[
p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{N-j,c}(x_0)
\geq p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{N-k,c}(x_0),
\quad
\mathcal R_j\subseteq\mathcal R_k,
\quad
b_j\leq b_k.
\tag{9}
\]
For any vector \(v\in\mathbb R^N\), written in increasing order as \(v_{(1)}\leq\cdots\leq v_{(N)}\), elementary counting gives, for \(r<N\),
\[
\sum_{u=1}^N\mathbf 1\{v_u>c\}>r
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
v_{(N-r)}>c.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus, unless a rejected \(r=N\) null has already made the intersection empty, the definition of \(\mathcal C_\alpha\), (8), and (10) give
\[
\theta\in\mathcal C_\alpha
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\theta_{(j)}(e)>c
\text{ for every }c\in\mathcal R_j
\text{ and every }j=1,\ldots,N.
\tag{11}
\]

Suppose first that \(\mathcal C_\alpha\neq\varnothing\).  Equation (11) implies \(\theta_{(k)}(e)\geq b_k\) for every \(\theta\in\mathcal C_\alpha\), so \(\ell_k(e;\alpha)\geq b_k\).  If \(b_k\) is finite, (9) permits a nondecreasing effect vector whose first \(k\) coordinates equal \(b_k+\eta\), with later coordinates chosen recursively above the corresponding finite \(b_j\).  It satisfies (11), and it is realized by setting \(\theta_u(0,e)=0\) and \(\theta_u(1,e)\) equal to its coordinates.  Letting \(\eta\downarrow0\) proves \(\ell_k(e;\alpha)\leq b_k\).  If \(b_k=-\infty\), then (9) makes \(\mathcal R_j\) empty for \(j\leq k\); choosing the first \(k\) effects equal to \(-M\) and letting \(M\to\infty\) proves the same equality.  Therefore
\[
\ell_k(e;\alpha)=b_k
\quad\text{whenever }\mathcal C_\alpha\neq\varnothing.
\tag{12}
\]

It remains to verify (12) when the confidence region is empty.  For fixed \(r\), let \(\mathcal Q_r(c)\) be the finite set of assignment-wide rank patterns attainable by schedules in \(\Theta_{r,c}(x_0,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Since increasing \(c\) weakens the exceedance-count restriction,
\[
c_1\leq c_2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal Q_r(c_1)\subseteq\mathcal Q_r(c_2).
\tag{13}
\]
Every observation-compatible finite schedule belongs to \(\Theta_{r,c}\) once \(c\) exceeds its largest direct effect.  Because the total set of rank patterns is finite, there is a finite \(c_0\) such that
\[
\mathcal Q_r(c)=\mathcal Q_N(c)
\quad\text{for every }c\geq c_0.
\tag{14}
\]
This is the required finite-cell stabilization.

If some \(\mathcal R_j\) is unbounded above, monotonicity in \(c\) implies \(p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{N-j,c}(x_0)\leq\alpha\) for every \(c\).  By (6), (7), and (14), its stabilized value is the worst-case value over all compatible schedules, which is exactly the value for \(r=N\).  Therefore
\[
p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{N,c}(x_0)\leq\alpha
\quad\text{for every }c.
\tag{15}
\]
The rejected \(r=N\) constraint in \(\mathcal C_\alpha\) is the empty set.  Moreover, every \(\Theta_{N-k,c}\) is contained in \(\Theta_{N,c}\), so (15) implies \(\mathcal R_k=\mathbb R\) and \(b_k=+\infty\) for all \(k\).  Conversely, if there is no rejected \(r=N\) constraint and every \(b_j<+\infty\), one can recursively choose a nondecreasing finite vector strictly above all thresholds in the sets \(\mathcal R_j\), realize it as a schedule, and satisfy (11); hence the region is nonempty.  Thus every empty-region case gives
\[
\ell_k(e;\alpha)=\inf_{\theta\in\varnothing}\theta_{(k)}(e)
=+\infty=b_k,
\qquad k=1,\ldots,N.
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (12) and (16) prove the projection identity in all cases.

For simultaneous coverage, let \(Y\) denote the true fixed schedule and set
\[
p^Y(x):=p_K(x;s_Y).
\tag{17}
\]
The outcome-free kernel, fixed schedule, and fixed statistic make (17) a deterministic score-vector randomization value.  The subset inequalities and the universal-validity theorem imply
\[
\Pr_{X\sim\pi}\{p^Y(X)\leq\alpha\}\leq\alpha.
\tag{18}
\]
If \(Y\notin\mathcal C_\alpha\), then some rejected pair \((r,c)\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{u\in U}\mathbf 1\{\tau_u(e)>c\}\leq r.
\tag{19}
\]
At every realized assignment, observation consistency and (19) put the true schedule in \(\Theta_{r,c}(X,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\).  The defining supremum therefore gives
\[
p^Y(X)\leq p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(X)\leq\alpha.
\tag{20}
\]
Thus \(\{Y\notin\mathcal C_\alpha\}\subseteq\{p^Y(X)\leq\alpha\}\), and (18) yields \(\Pr\{Y\in\mathcal C_\alpha\}\geq1-\alpha\).  On this event, the definition of an infimum gives
\[
\tau_{(k)}(e)=Y_{(k)}(e)
\geq\inf_{\theta\in\mathcal C_\alpha}\theta_{(k)}(e)
=\ell_k(e;\alpha)
\quad\text{for all }k,
\tag{21}
\]
which proves the asserted joint coverage.  This common-sharp-schedule domination also contains the established per-null composite validity as a special case.

Finally, (10) proves the stated no-interference order-statistic equivalence, and partition kernels remain valid by the universal-validity characterization.  Exact equality with the two cited comparator statistics is a different assertion.  The comparator-obstruction proposition supplies the two-unit, one-treated example stated in the theorem: the frozen score uses assignment-specific outcome vectors \((3,0)\) and \((1,2)\), giving treated rank two at both assignments and hence tail mass \(1\), while subtraction of the boundary value \(2\) fixes the adjusted vector \((1,0)\), giving treated ranks two and one and tail mass \(1/2\).  The one-stratum Su--Li case contains the same example.  Therefore the finite network reduction, order-statistic equivalence, validity, and simultaneous projection are proved, while exact recovery of those comparator algorithms, and hence the claimed strict extension of both, is refuted.
theorem.justification: This theorem closes the finite assignment-coupled schedule optimization and simultaneous within-exposure projection while explicitly isolating the comparator mismatch.
theorem.gap: Existing no-interference reductions do not enforce one shared potential-outcome schedule across network assignments, and their adjusted-outcome scores are not identical to the frozen assignment-specific score.
theorem.consumer: On a predeclared imputable Cai--Owusu exposure fiber, the theorem yields exact worst-case bounded-null values and simultaneous lower bounds, subject to the separately required empirical fiber and power checks.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 proves super-uniformity for conditional randomization tests induced by a finite partition of the assignment space.
Theorem 2 makes arbitrary permutation laws valid by introducing an independent random reference permutation.
Biclique conditioning yields valid exact tests on imputable assignment subsets under general interference.
A power proxy under normality and constant effects guides refinement of biclique decompositions.

Theorem 4 gives individual effect-quantile confidence sets under exchangeable treatment and Section 5.5 gives a simultaneous construction; the frozen assignment-specific schedule score is not their adjusted-outcome statistic.
The paper gives finite-sample improvements for individual-effect distributions and quantiles in completely randomized, stratified randomized, sampling-based, and matched designs.

Theorems 1 and 3 give exact stratified quantile-null tests, a multiple-choice-knapsack computation, and simultaneous inversion; the frozen assignment-specific schedule score does not reduce to that knapsack statistic.
Theorem 1 establishes asymptotic validity for a class of network heterogeneity randomization tests with adaptive focal assignments.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact network schedule reduction is now proved, but the two-unit witness refutes exact recovery of the Caughey and Su--Li score computations.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite conditional randomization law need not resample from a partition cell. Universal validity of an arbitrary legal row kernel is characterized exactly by the inequalities \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\), with an equivalent peeling core, an \(O(m2^m)\) separator, and a finite union-of-polyhedra design region. A three-state directed-cycle fiber certifies exact power \(2/3\) for a valid nonpartition kernel versus zero for every legal partition kernel. On a predeclared network-exposure fiber, finite weak-order enumeration with strict-cell linear feasibility computes every worst-case bounded-null value and its optimizing schedule, and nested inversion gives simultaneous lower bounds for all exposure-specific effect quantiles. This exact network reduction does not reproduce the adjusted-outcome computations of Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix or Su--Li; a two-unit example gives frozen and comparator values \(1\) and \(1/2\), respectively.

project_justification.gap: Conditional randomization under interference is operationally partition-based, while arbitrary-permutation validity relies on auxiliary symmetrization. No-interference quantile methods provide important inversion templates, but their adjusted-outcome score reductions do not enforce one shared potential-outcome schedule across network assignments and are not identical to the frozen assignment-specific score.
project_justification.niche: Finite directed legal supports permit overlapping row kernels whose validity and power can be decided before outcomes are observed, while finite weak-order cells preserve the shared potential-outcome constraints needed for exact network effect-quantile inference.
project_justification.fill: The project gives exact row-kernel validity geometry, a worked directed-cycle certificate with a strict partition power gap, certified power design, a terminating exact weak-order and linear-feasibility reduction for bounded-null schedules, and simultaneous within-exposure quantile projection. It also gives an explicit obstruction to claiming exact recovery of the Caughey or Su--Li computational statistics.

prose_updates.related_work: Zhang and Zhao (2023) formulate conditional randomization through assignment-space partitions and prove validity by a conditional probability-integral transform; their partition kernel is strictly contained in the score-uniform row-kernel characterization. Ramdas et al. (2023) validate arbitrary nonuniform permutation laws after a random reference permutation restores exchangeability, a different construction from an unmodified deterministic row kernel. Puelz et al. (2022) encode imputability through null-exposure graphs and bicliques, which supply legal network fibers, while Yanagi and Sei (2022) use an approximate model-based power expression to refine biclique selection. Caughey et al. (2023, Theorem 4 and Section 5.5) provide individual and simultaneous no-interference effect-quantile inference under exchangeable treatment, and Su and Li (2024) provide stratified quantile tests and a multiple-choice-knapsack computation. Their order-statistic null equivalence and inversion logic inform the present construction, but the frozen score evaluates assignment-specific imputed outcomes rather than a fixed adjusted-outcome vector; the explicit two-unit witness therefore rules out exact computational recovery of either method. Chen and Li's 2026 finite-sample improvements likewise concern no-interference complete, stratified, sampling-based, or matched designs. Owusu (2023) studies network heterogeneous-effect randomization tests with adaptive focal assignments; the Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet weather-insurance reanalysis is the intended empirical consumer, not evidence for the theorem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact schedule solver is finite but exponential, with at most \(2^N3^{m\binom N2}\) raw effect/sign labels before pruning. Ordinary terminating computation requires rational or real-algebraic representations of kernel weights, outcomes, thresholds, levels, and the finite rank-score table; arbitrary real constants support only an ideal exact-real formulation. The universal-validity geometry also does not guarantee useful power on every legal support. The Cai application must stop if its imputable fiber is too small, its legal support forces partition kernels, or its certified partition power gap is zero.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The universal iff, recursion, peeling equivalence, polyhedral representation, finite kernel optimizer, strict three-state inclusion and power witnesses, minimal coupled pattern, and composite-null validity are theorem-level results. The network schedule problem is closed by finite weak-order enumeration and strict-cell linear feasibility; for nonempty null schedule sets it returns an optimizing schedule, while empty sets are certified infeasible. Nested inversion yields exact simultaneous lower bounds for all effect quantiles at one predeclared exposure, including the empty-region convention through finite-cell stabilization. The no-interference count null is exactly an order-statistic null and partition kernels remain valid, but the frozen assignment-specific score does not equal the Caughey adjusted-outcome statistic or the Su--Li knapsack statistic, so neither algorithm is claimed as an exact specialization. Cross-exposure simultaneity and an actual Cai--Owusu power gain remain outside the theorem and require, respectively, explicit level allocation and empirical fiber computation.

proofs.proof_tex:
Because \(Y_u(a,e')\) is constant in \(e'\), the quantity
\[
 \tau_u(e)=Y_u(1,e)-Y_u(0,e)
\]
is the ordinary individual treatment effect and does not depend on the exposure label.  Write its ordered coordinates as
\(\tau_{(1)}(e)\leq\cdots\leq\tau_{(N)}(e)\).  If \(r<N\), at most \(r\) coordinates exceed \(c\) if and only if at least \(N-r\) coordinates are at most \(c\).  By the definition of an order statistic, the latter condition is equivalent to \(\tau_{(N-r)}(e)\leq c\).  Hence
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}\mathbf 1\{\tau_u(e)>c\}\leq r
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \tau_{(N-r)}(e)\leq c.
\]
When \(r=N\), the left side is bounded above by \(|U|=N\) identically, so that null is vacuous.  This proves the asserted causal-null interpretation, including the strict threshold convention: effects equal to \(c\) are not counted as exceeding \(c\).

We next verify the partition-kernel certificate rather than assuming it.  Let \(\mathcal G\) be any finite partition of \(\Omega\), and define
\[
 K(x,B)=\frac{\pi(B\cap G_x)}{\pi(G_x)}.
\]
Every cell is nonempty, and \(\pi(x)>0\) for every \(x\) by \(\texttt{ass:positive-finite-design}\); consequently \(\pi(G_x)>0\), so the displayed division is defined.  The cells partition \(\Omega\), and therefore
\[
 \sum_{y\in\Omega}K(x,y)
 =\frac{\pi(G_x)}{\pi(G_x)}=1,
\]
which proves row-stochasticity.  Fix a nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\) and an arbitrary ordering \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Ord}(A)\).  For every cell \(H\in\mathcal G\) with \(A\cap H\neq\varnothing\), let \(j_H\) be the index at which the last element of \(A\cap H\) appears in \(\sigma\).  Since every prefix is contained in \(A\),
\[
 P_{j_H}(\sigma)\cap H=A\cap H,
\]
and hence
\[
 K\bigl(\sigma_{j_H},P_{j_H}(\sigma)\bigr)
 =\frac{\pi(A\cap H)}{\pi(H)}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq |A|}K(\sigma_j,P_j(\sigma))
 \geq
 \max_{H\in\mathcal G:\,A\cap H\neq\varnothing}
 \frac{\pi(A\cap H)}{\pi(H)}
 \geq
 \sum_{H\in\mathcal G}\pi(H)
 \frac{\pi(A\cap H)}{\pi(H)}
 =\pi(A).
\]
In the middle expression a cell disjoint from \(A\) is assigned ratio zero; the second inequality is the fact that a weighted average, with nonnegative weights \(\pi(H)\) summing to one, cannot exceed its largest entry.  The ordering \(\sigma\) was arbitrary, so minimizing over orderings as in \(\texttt{def:subset-degeneracy}\) gives
\[
 d_K(A)\geq\pi(A).
\]
The one-cell complete-randomization kernel and the within-stratum conditional kernel in the statement are both instances of this calculation.  Thus \(\texttt{thm:universal-validity-iff}\) makes each kernel universally valid.  Under the fixed-schedule, outcome-free, fixed-exposure, and imputability conditions stated in the proposition, \(\texttt{thm:composite-null-validity}\) then yields, for every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \Pr_{X\sim\pi}\{p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(X)\leq\alpha\}\leq\alpha
\]
whenever the true schedule lies in \(\Theta_{r,c}(X,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\).  This is finite-sample validity of the frozen test for the causal null just characterized.  Separately, the comparator-specific individual and simultaneous confidence conclusions are supplied by the cited leaves \(\texttt{lem:caughey-quantile-specialization}\) and \(\texttt{lem:suli-knapsack-specialization}\); those leaves concern their own comparator constructions and do not assert equality with \(\texttt{def:schedule-score}\).

It remains to prove that the claimed exact reductions fail.  Take \(N=2\) and let \(x_i\) denote the assignment treating unit \(i\) and not the other unit.  Set
\[
 \Omega=\{x_1,x_2\},\qquad
 \pi(x_1)=\pi(x_2)=\frac12,\qquad
 K(x_i,x_j)=\frac12\quad(1\leq i,j\leq2).
\]
For a singleton \(A=\{x_i\}\), \(d_K(A)=1/2=\pi(A)\); for \(A=\Omega\), every ordering has prefix masses \(1/2\) and \(1\), so \(d_K(\Omega)=1=\pi(\Omega)\).  Thus this smallest complete-randomization design satisfies the universal-validity certificate exactly.

Choose \(\phi(j)=j\), set \(T=T_{\mathrm C}\), and, for every \(e'\in\mathcal E\), define the fixed no-interference schedule
\[
 \theta_1(0,e')=1,\quad \theta_1(1,e')=3,
 \qquad
 \theta_2(0,e')=0,\quad \theta_2(1,e')=2.
\]
Suppose \(X=x_1\).  Then \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=(3,0)\).  Under \(x_1\), the imputed outcome vector is \((3,0)\), and treated unit one has ascending rank two.  Under \(x_2\), the imputed outcome vector is \((1,2)\), and treated unit two also has ascending rank two.  There are no ties, so the predeclared tie rule is immaterial.  By \(\texttt{def:caughey-rank-score}\) and \(\texttt{def:schedule-score}\),
\[
 s_{\theta}(x_1)=2=s_{\theta}(x_2).
\]
Therefore \(\texttt{def:kernel-tail-value}\) gives
\[
 p_K(x_1;s_{\theta})
 =\frac12\mathbf 1\{2\geq2\}
  +\frac12\mathbf 1\{2\geq2\}=1.
\]
Both individual effects equal \(2\), so
\[
 \sum_{u=1}^{2}\mathbf 1\{\theta_u(1,e)-\theta_u(0,e)>2\}=0.
\]
The schedule is consistent with the observed outcomes at \(x_1\), hence \(\theta\in\Theta_{0,2}(x_1,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\).  By \(\texttt{def:worst-case-pvalue}\),
\[
 p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{0,2}(x_1)
 \geq p_K(x_1;s_{\theta})=1.
\]
Since a supremum of values in \([0,1]\) is at most one, equality follows:
\[
 p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{0,2}(x_1)=1.
\]

For the Caughey adjusted-outcome construction at boundary \(c=2\), instead hold fixed, across reallocations, the observed adjusted vector
\[
 a=Y^{\mathrm{obs}}-2\bigl(Z_1(x_1),Z_2(x_1)\bigr)=(1,0).
\]
The treated unit has rank two under \(x_1\) and rank one under \(x_2\), so
\[
 T_{\mathrm C}(x_1,a)=2,
 \qquad T_{\mathrm C}(x_2,a)=1.
\]
Its upper-tail randomization value at \(x_1\) is consequently
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^{2}\pi(x_j)
 \mathbf 1\{T_{\mathrm C}(x_j,a)\geq T_{\mathrm C}(x_1,a)\}
 =\frac12,
\]
which differs from the frozen value one.  Finally, take one stratum, \(S=1\), \(U_1=U\), and \(\phi_1=\phi\).  Then the within-stratum ranks are the full-sample ranks and \(T_{\mathrm S}=T_{\mathrm C}\), so the same \(1\)-versus-\(1/2\) discrepancy applies to the one-stratum Su--Li construction.  This explicit witness proves that the frozen schedule score does not exactly recover either comparator, while leaving intact the order-statistic equivalence and the finite-sample validity proved above.
